about: Own-words reads from the daily research task (ADMIS, Rabobank, Czapp and the news feed). fund_score: -1 bearish to +1 bullish, a judgement on the fundamental news only.

cotton.fundamental: Mar is choppy around 81.5-82 in thin pre-holiday trade, giving back part of Tuesday's outside-market lift early before steadying. Nothing new on demand; old-crop Mar/May still leans on Texas Plains losses, while Dec delivery and high-grade certs keep the risk two-sided for longs.
events: Cotton fades in early Wednesday trade (Barchart)
Mar ~82 midday in light holiday volume (ICE/Yahoo Finance)
Broad risk-off as equities slide and VIX jumps to ~34 (WSJ, Yahoo Finance)

sugar.fundamental: Mar has extended to about 18.28 (+0.9%), back above its 100-day average, as the real firms close to 2% to ~5.82 per dollar, which further cuts Brazilian mills' appetite to hedge exports. There is still no fresh centre-south crush or mix data, and the surprise US tariff proposal on Brazil matters little for sugar flows, so the Brazil supply picture is unchanged and the move is currency and short covering.
events: Raw sugar Mar ~18.28, through 18.17 resistance (ICE/Yahoo Finance)
Real strengthens ~1.9% vs the dollar (Yahoo Finance)
Dollar weakness spurs short covering in sugar (Barchart)

coffee.fundamental: Dec arabica eased about 1% to ~265.7 early, still near four-month lows, even with a firmer real. The certified-stock build from Brazilian arabica heading into ICE warehouses remains the dominant factor for Dec/Mar deliverability. A new US tariff proposal on Brazil is a watch point: coffee was spared in July, and if it is included it would steer US buyers away from Brazilian beans and slow the flow into US-delivered certs.
events: US proposes surprise new tariffs on Brazilian imports, incl. 10% on aircraft (Reuters)
Brazilian arabica heading to ICE warehouses (Finimize, CNN Brasil)

cocoa.fundamental: Latest reports point to Ivory Coast port arrivals running slower again, which lifted prices on Tuesday and cuts against the ample-supply story; rising ICE certified stocks are the main offset. No new Ghana COCOBOD news, and the ICCO November quarterly bulletin is not yet out.
events: Cocoa climbs as Ivory Coast shipments decline (Barchart)
EUDR preparations lift European cocoa premiums (Bloomberg)
